summary: Thomas Adams Borchert works in Buddhist and religious studies. A PhD candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2005), he studied under Bruce Lincoln, Alan Berkowitz, and Donald K. Swearer, among others. He was Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Thomas B. Ellis works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and served as Assistant Professor of Religion in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).

Thomas Burrow (1909–1986) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Cambridge, SOAS, and Annamalai, studying under E. J. Rapson and P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri. He held posts at the British Museum and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1944–1976).

Thomas Christian Tychsen (1758–1834) was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel University (circa 1777–1779) and the University of Göttingen (circa 1779–1783), where he later held a post from circa 1784 to 1834.

Thomas Cleary (1949–2021) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earned a Ph.D. from Harvard University, and obtained a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.

Thomas Doctor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche, Christian K. Wedemeyer, and Tom Tillemans at the University of Lausanne, and at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling. He held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Thomas E. Crow (born 1948) is an art historian educated at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, served as director of the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and joined NYU as professor in 2007.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke (1813–1890) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology educated at Eton College and East India Company College. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Thomas Ethelbert Page (1850–1936) was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He was educated at Shrewsbury School (circa 1864–1869) and St John's College (circa 1869–1873), and later held a post at Charterhouse School from 1899 to 1936.

Thomas F. Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and Columbia University (PhD 2003) under Robert A. F. Thurman and others, later serving as Executive Editor in Columbia's Department of Religion (attested 2007).

Thomas J. Mazanec works in sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Calvin University, the University of Colorado Boulder (MA), and Princeton University (PhD), he studied under Anna M. Shields, Stephen F. Teiser, Paul W. Kroll, and Ping Wang, among others.

Thomas Jülch (born 1975) works in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, University of Hull (MA), Heidelberg University, and the University of Munich (PhD circa 2006–2011), later serving as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2013–2019).

Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held a post at City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).

Thomas Oberlies (born 1960) is an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme. He held a post at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001) and an Arbeitsstellenleiter post at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Thomas R. Trautmann (born 1940) is an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as professor of history and anthropology at the University of Michigan (attested 1991).

Thomas Roebuck (1781–1819) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the Royal High School. He was assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George (1811) and a member of the Asiatic Society (circa 1811–1819).

Thomas Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) was an administrator and scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He joined the East India Company in 1795, founded the Zoological Society of London (1825–1825), and served as its president in 1826.

Thomas Watters (1840–1901) was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at Queen's University Belfast, Queen's University of Ireland, and Queen's University at Kingston, earning B.A. degrees circa 1861.

Thomas William Rhys Davids (1843–1922) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau (PhD). He founded the Pali Text Society, held posts at UCL and London, and held the Comparative Religion chair at Manchester (1904–1915).

Thomas Yūhō Kirchner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held a professorship at Hanazono University (attested 2001) and a post at the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (attested 2006).
